notes: New: the Obsidian Generator makes obsidian from lava and water: 1 block every 10 seconds for 400 power, 8 obsidian per lava bucket. Feed it lava buckets (by hand, in its screen or by pipe; the empty buckets come back) or let it touch a Tank or Lava Pump. Water comes free from a touching water source block, or from a touching Tank of water (1 bucket per 8 obsidian). It takes Speed and Efficiency Chips and has Steel and Deepcore tiers, like the other machines. Also in 4.65.0: Other add-ons can now give Deepcore pictures of their items for crate fronts (the dq:add_icon script event, see docs/addon-api.md on GitHub). Until an add-on does, its items still store normally and show a ? plate. Also in 4.64.0: Crates now show a picture for every Deepcore block and item on their front (Network Cable, Deepcore Chest, tanks, suit parts, reactor and portal blocks and more showed a "?"), and cables and pipes show a cable or pipe instead of a jumbled texture. Also in 4.63.0: Water buckets can go into the Network Terminal now (dropped on a cell or shift-clicked), and so can other plain items that don't stack, like milk and powder snow buckets, saddles, minecarts, boats and cakes. Items that would lose something when stored (named items, potions, books, maps, shulker boxes, mob buckets, tools and armour) are handed back, and the terminal now says it can't take them instead of pointing to an i tab it doesn't have. Also in 4.62.0: the Network Terminal, Network Crafter and Deepcore Crafting Table now take one player at a time, so two people no longer move each other's items or searches. While someone uses one, anyone else who taps it is told who is using it, and gets it as soon as that player looks away. Each player keeps their own view: search, sort and page on the terminal, search and pick on the Crafter, tab, search and recipe on the crafting table. Items you laid in the crafting table's grid by hand come back to you as soon as you look away. Also in 4.61.0: Other add-ons can now plug into Deepcore. They can send Deepcore their crafting recipes (dq:add_recipe), so their items can be ordered from the Network Crafter, made by Assemblers and crafted at the Deepcore Crafting Table, and they can register their ores (dq:add_ore), so the Geo Scanner, its hologram and the Mining Suit's Ore Sense count them with their own name and colour. Nothing changes if no add-on sends them. Also in 4.60.0: Lava buckets put into the network are kept now. Before, a lava bucket put in through the Network Terminal (dropped on a cell or shift-clicked) was lost when no crate already held lava buckets, and dropping one on the empty-bucket cell left you with the empty buckets and no lava. Lava buckets now go into an empty crate or a free Deepcore Chest slot, and anything the network cannot store comes back to you. Also in 4.59.0: Shift-click now puts items into the Network Terminal, even when the page is full of items (it had no empty slot to land in). Items the network has no room for go back to you. Also in 4.58.0: the network merges part stacks of the same item across its Deepcore Chests, so one item no longer takes a slot in every chest. Earlier: Network Terminal search works like the crafting table's and the Network Crafter's: tap Search, type a name (and pick the sort) in the box, then tap the terminal again for the results. Show all clears the search. Also in 4.56.0: the Network Crafter has a Show all button next to Search: it clears the search and shows everything the network can make. Also in 4.55.0: Network Terminal: every item shows how many the whole network holds right on its slot, like a crate's front (8.1k); point at it for the exact number. Taking one still gives a stack. Also in 4.53.0: items you put in a networked Deepcore Chest now move by themselves into a networked crate that already holds (or is locked to) the same item, while that crate has room. Also in 4.52.0: the Network Cable has a new look (black cable with green lights).
